title: .deliver.json — how /deliver runs in this repository
description: Per-repo settings for the deliver plugin. Deep-merged over the kit defaults (kit/skills/deliver/config.json). `dl config` shows what applies; a running job keeps the snapshot it took at `dl new`. Reference: docs/03-settings.md.

dispatch.description: munder (default): every role is a person at a seat on the Munder Difflin floor; /deliver in a terminal opens the app and hands the job to Michael there. subagent: roles run as Claude Code subagents in one claude session (no app; required for unattended runs). Chosen by the human; Michael never switches it.

base_branch.description: Branch the job starts from and the PR targets (auto = the main checkout's current branch).

record_job.description: dl ship commits the job's record to .deliver/jobs/<job>/ with its code: the request, the readiness decisions and their sources, the plan, the specs, the board (every gate, QA and review verdict), the report and the event log — the audit trail in git. false keeps it in .work/ only.

qa_verify_full.description: A QA pass also runs verify_full on the card's commit, with the dev's and QA's tests together, before review — catches tests that pass alone but break the suite together (e.g. two helpers with the same module name). When the architecture gives the card's component its own suite (readiness.json components[].verify), that one runs instead. false only for a suite too slow to run per card; verify_full still runs on the job branch at the end.

risk.description: Risk-based test design: every acceptance criterion of the plan carries a priority [P0]…[P3]; each card spec has a "## Test design" (per AC: priority, level, scenarios); a QA pass names a result for every AC of the card; every decided non-functional requirement (readiness NFR-*) is in the plan and gets PASS / CONCERNS / FAIL in the closing report — anything but PASS ships only with dl waive, listed in the PR.

blind.description: A blind review: a reviewer who sees only the diff — no card, no spec, no QA result — judges what the code does. risk: cards with a P0 or P1 acceptance criterion; all: every card; off: none. Michael triages each finding against the spec: intended (the spec's words quoted) or a defect for the dev.

max_cards.description: The light path (dl track light: a small change inside existing code) plans at most this many cards; a bigger job goes to the full path (dl track full).

engine.description: Shaping before the readiness review. auto: only a request that is not a specification yet — it states fewer than two of requirement ids, acceptance criteria and a contract (measured live: on a specified request shaping cost 30 % more for the same product; on an idea it caught decisions the readiness review missed). bmad: every full-path job. the BMad Method (installed into the repo, outside git) chooses its own path and writes the specification headless from the request, the repo, the standards and our delivery checklist; every decision, assumption, question and review finding it reports is decided by Michael with the human, sent back to BMad, and frozen with the readiness decisions at planning. off: the readiness review works from the request alone.

bmad_version.description: The BMad Method release dl shape install installs (npx bmad-method@<version>); its output formats are read by bin/bmad.mjs.

review_rounds.description: How many times bmad-review reviews the artifacts (after the decisions went back to BMad). 0: no review.

reask_rounds.description: How often the decisions go back to the same artifacts before BMad makes something new or reviews. Past it, the decisions bind through the shaping ledger and the PR lists them as such (an update that keeps raising questions on what it was just told cannot hold shaping forever).

model.description: The model of the BMad sessions (claude --model); empty: Claude Code's default.

timeout_min.description: A BMad session that runs longer is stopped and counted as a failed run.

merge_verify.description: Right after dl integrate, the job branch runs the merged card's component suite (readiness.json components[].verify), so the card that breaks it is named at once and a fix card opened. Only for components with their own suite; false turns it off (verify-all still runs at the end).

keep_awake.description: While dl runs tests the machine does not sleep (macOS caffeinate, Linux systemd-inhibit, Windows SetThreadExecutionState); the hold ends with that dl run. false turns it off.

checkpoints.description: Headless (scripts/run-headless.sh): Michael ends his session at every phase change and after every wave of cards (dl checkpoint) and the next round goes on in a fresh one, so his context stays small. false: one session runs as long as it can.

ports.description: The project's names for the ports its test setup starts servers on, each an offset into a test run's 50 ports: {"WEB_PORT": 0, "API_PORT": 1} gives T-07's run WEB_PORT=20700 and API_PORT=20701, its QA worktree 20750 and 20751, the job branch 20000 and 20001. dl exports them for every test run and dl env prints them; the test setup reads them (old port as fallback), so a frontend and a backend card's QA run side by side instead of waiting for each other.

verify_full.description: The full test suite, run on the job branch after every card merged (what your CI runs). Detected from the repo when /deliver writes this file; in a repo without code it is set once the stack is decided.

worktree_setup.description: Runs in every new card worktree (install deps, copy .env, …).

worktree_exclude.description: Paths worktree_setup creates that never count as changes.

merge_mode.description: human: a PR you merge · semi: auto-merge armed, you approve · auto: merged on green CI · local: merged into the base branch locally, no remote.

max_parallel.description: Cards running at once (all roles together).

qa_early.description: QA writes each card's tests from its spec while the developer builds it (own worktree; joined after the gate with dl qa-join), instead of after the gate.

max_attempts.description: Tries per card before it is blocked and Michael decides (split, replace or drop — listed in the PR).

plan.description: true: you approve the plan and board before any code.

gate_timeout.description: Seconds a card's verify / qa_verify may run.

roles.description: Project defaults per role, applied when Michael picks the roles. A role entry that names its own value (from the request's Staffing, or what you tell Michael at the start) keeps it. Role names: ba, backend, frontend, mobile, database, qa, backend-lead, frontend-lead, reviewer-<stack>, security, accessibility, performance, …

model.description: e.g. opus, sonnet, haiku, or another CLI's model (gpt-5-codex).

provider.description: Which CLI runs the role (non-Claude needs dispatch munder).

count.description: Seats of this role working in parallel (backend#1, backend#2 …).

hive_root.description: The Munder Difflin hive folder for this repo (the app's harnessHome). /deliver opens the app on it.

app_command.description: How to start Munder Difflin when it is not running (default: the installed app, or `npm run preview` in the source checkout scripts/init.sh made).

model.description: Model of every Claude seat whose role names none. Seats never start on the app's default model.

seat_timeout_minutes.description: A seat with no 'seated' message this long after hiring is failed (dl md-seats says why; Michael re-seats it).

claude_command.description: Command the Claude seats run (a wrapper or pinned path).

kind.description: local (kanban + kanban.html), jira, asana, linear, github (GitHub Projects), or a registered tracker plugin.

columns.description: Your board's own names for the stages: todo, in_progress, qa, review, done, blocked, wontdo (default To Do, In Progress, QA, Code Review, Done, Blocked, Won't Do).

jira.description: project (key), issue_type, epic_type, labels, api_version. Credentials: JIRA_BASE_URL + JIRA_EMAIL + JIRA_API_TOKEN, or JIRA_PAT.

project.description: The project's gid (from its URL); its sections are the columns.

team.description: The team's key (e.g. ENG); its workflow states are the columns.

repo.description: owner/name — where the issues are opened.

project.description: The project (v2) number, from its URL.

project_owner.description: The organization or user that owns the project (default: the repo's owner).

status_field.description: The project's single-select field whose options are the columns.

labels.description: Labels put on every issue (they must exist in the repo).

github.description: Credentials: GITHUB_TOKEN (or GH_TOKEN) with access to the repo's issues and the project.

knowledge.description: The shared knowledge repo — standards and lessons several projects share. dl new clones it (into ~/.deliver/shared/) and updates it at every job's start; shared lessons are proposed to it as a PR. Without it, each project keeps its own in .deliver/knowledge/.

repo.description: git URL or path of the shared knowledge repo (standards/*.md, lessons.md).

branch.description: Its branch (default: the clone's default branch).

convention.description: The repo's commit message convention — every commit of a job follows it (the devs', QA's and dl's own merges; the gate checks the card's commits, with the repo's own commitlint when installed). Detected when this file is written: commitlint / commitizen / a commit-msg hook, else the history.

merge_message.description: The message of dl's merge commits, when the convention's default forms are refused by the repo's hooks: {card}, {title} and {key} (the tracker key) are filled in. Empty: dl picks a form that fits the convention.

ai_attribution.description: false: commits must not carry AI attribution (the gate checks).

role_in_message.description: true: every card commit carries a 'Role: <seat>' trailer.
